root_idea.summary: The root centers on lowering and humble submission, especially an inward state of reverent yielding.
root_idea.development: Its concrete point of departure is خَبْتٌ, a low or depressed tract of ground. The derived verb develops from directing oneself toward or entering such a low place to the figurative sense of becoming lowly, gentle, and submissive before God.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form أَخْبَتَ.
Displayed under the singular active-participle citation form مُخْبِتٌ; the supplied Quran occurrence is its plural.

senses.definition: To become lowly, humble, submissive, and obedient; to humble oneself and turn trustfully toward God.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic constructions أَخْبَتُوا إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ and فَتُخْبِتَ لَهُ قُلُوبُهُمْ, the verb expresses inward submission to God. With hearts as subject, it denotes their becoming soft and reverently humble; the preposition may convey direction or dedication toward Him.

senses.definition: A person humble and submissive before God; one whose heart is softened in reverent submission.
senses.usage_conditions: Active participle of Form IV, occurring in the Quran in the masculine plural مُخْبِتِينَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a person's or thing's mention or reputation to become concealed, obscure, or without repute.
In a reported dialectal or traditional usage, to be bad or corrupt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Equated in the lexical entry with خَبُثَ; this is distinct from the Form IV Quranic sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To head toward or descend into a خَبْتٌ, a low or depressed tract of ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A literal spatial use of the Form IV verb, distinct from its Quranic figurative use of humble submission.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A low or depressed tract of ground, including a broad plain, sandy lowland, valley bottom, or deep valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term covers several kinds of spacious or low terrain, including soft or concealed low ground.
A figurative abstract noun for the state of being lowly or submissive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Contemptible, base, bad, corrupt, vile, or disapproved; a contemptible or morally bad thing or person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied both to things and to persons. The form is reported as a dialectal variant or equivalent of خَبِيثٌ, with textual uncertainty in the cited material.
A rare reported use, distinct from the Quranic active-participle sense of humble submission.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The construction concerning a mention becoming obscure is represented.
The reported dialectal bad/corrupt sense is represented.
The literal relation of أَخْبَتَ to خَبْتٌ is represented.
The Quran-attested humble, submissive, and obedient use is represented.
The terrain noun and its lowland/valley applications are represented.
The abstract noun for lowliness and humility is represented.
The contemptible, bad, or vile sense is represented.
The application of the same sense to a person is covered.
The reported still or motionless use is represented separately.

cautions: The Form IV Quran citation is normalized to the dictionary form أَخْبَتَ, and the Quranic nominal is normalized from مُخْبِتِينَ to مُخْبِتٌ.
The rare خَبِيتٌ entry is retained separately because its relation to خَبِيثٌ and the cited wording are reported with dialectal or textual uncertainty.
Historical citation notation in the lexical evidence is not used as a modern verse location; Quran examples follow the independently supplied QAC locations.
